**How to read this FAQ:** items **1–13** set definitions and entry surfaces; **14–23** cover process and compliance tone; **24–27** are short “technical honesty” checks for engineers and researchers (incl. fee-rail wording); **28–31** support partner-meeting depth Q&A (still not an offer).

---

### 1. What is TravelTrust?

A trust-oriented system for travel commerce: marketplace, orders, escrow, disputes, reputation, plus community and help. **On-chain Escrow, allocatable fee routing, and TTG (if any) boundaries** live in [02-Investor-Executive-Summary.md](02-Investor-Executive-Summary.md) and [06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md).

### 2. What is TravelTrust not?

Not a token-first narrative project, and not a landing page with fundraising story only. **Guide performance staking vs governance/TTG**—see **item 16** below.

### 3. vs traditional travel platforms?

Stronger emphasis on post-payment escrow, fulfillment, disputes, and reputation—not just discovery and payment.

### 4. vs typical Web3 projects?

We start from travel settlement and fulfillment, not from token lore that retrofits a product.

### 5. What is `/traveltrust`?

Brand and project landing for positioning; **not** a subscription or solicitation page.

### 6. What is `/market`?

The marketplace entry for supply and demand.

### 7. Why orders & escrow matter?

Trust is tested **after** payment: escrow, confirmation, ratings, disputes must work as one chain.

### 8. What does an Escrow path signal?

A closed loop from order to outcome—not only content.

### 9. Reputation layer?

Helps outsiders see how trust outcomes are surfaced.

### 10. Community & help?

Long-term operations and user education surfaces.

### 11. Are all URLs production?

Demo and staging may be used for product and investor meetings; do not equate with fully public production unless announced.

### 12. Fully launched?

We have a demonstrable core path; public release cadence follows **published announcements and environment labels**.

### 13. First touch for investors?

If you start from the **pitch deck**: **Deck → [01-OnePager.md](01-OnePager.md) (product spine) → this FAQ → live demo**; **governance, fee denominators, and TTG boundaries** are in [06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md) (read the **Abstract** and **§06** first, then expand as needed). Otherwise: **one-liner → one-pager → [04-PitchDeck-Storyboard.md](04-PitchDeck-Storyboard.md) (matches machine-built deck) → demo** also works.

### 14. First touch for partners?

Market, order/escrow path, reputation logic, community/help.

### 15. New community members?

Landing, market, FAQ first; not complex governance or fundraising on day one.

### 16. Guide “staking” vs governance “staking”?

**Different.** Guides: performance/onboarding mechanics. Governance: proposal/voting mechanics. Do not merge into one “staking coin” story.

### 17. Safest public narrative?

Trust-loop product system: market, escrow, disputes, reputation, community/help—no inflated launch claims, no impermissible return or equity promises.

### 18. Why so few hard numbers on One Pager / Deck?

Public materials emphasize **mechanism, stage, and policy**. Operating and financial figures need proper disclosure context; we share them **after NDA** with **traceable exports**, aligned by IR/Finance before meetings.

### 19. Are roadmap quarters a commitment?

**No.** Public language describes **direction and types of phase**. Binding obligations or investment terms require **signed agreements** under applicable law.

### 20. What “hard data” can we get?

Under confidentiality: metric tables, report excerpts, system exports—always with **environment** labels (demo / testnet / production). **Do not** present demo or test environments as full public production.

### 21. Where are you in a financing process?

As mutually discussed. **This FAQ does not describe live terms, valuation, or size.** Substantive terms belong in formal legal documents.

### 22. Beyond this pack?

Full DD and legal schedules are shared **as counsel agrees**; the public pack excludes cap tables, raw ledgers, and internal meeting notes.

### 23. Do public materials argue “you must invest now”?

**No.** Not a subscription urgency pitch or performance promise. If asked why not wait a year, the public stance only explains why funds often discuss **structural windows** alongside **execution readiness** (fragmented distribution, disclosure expectations on fund paths, maturing rails, etc.)—see the “Timing” section in [02-Investor-Executive-Summary.md](02-Investor-Executive-Summary.md) and **§2.4** in [06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md). **06** also contains a searchable block titled **“public boundary related to ‘revisit in one year’ (qualitative)”**; terms and cadence are governed by signed documents only.

### 24. Do you rely on bridges or external oracles?

**Follow public releases and contracts.** The whitepaper risk section states that bridges/oracles, **if used**, must sit inside security and audit scope (**06 §11.2**). **Do not verbally assume “live in prod”** for components not explicitly called out in public materials; confirm with environment labels and release notes, with engineering checklists under **NDA** if needed.

### 25. Who can upgrade contracts or hit pause / emergency controls?

Public stance is principles-only: **upgrade paths, keys, and multisig practice** must align with audit and governance processes (**06 §11.2**, **§08** roadmap narrative). **We do not list signer names or thresholds in this FAQ**; diligence should request runbooks, parameters, and change logs under **NDA**.

### 26. Is reputation “fully on-chain”?

**Hybrid model:** on-chain anchors **verifiable fulfillment and fund-state facts**; discovery, retrieval, and parts of UX can live off-chain—see **06 §05** and **§10.1**. Do not verbally equate a “ratings UI” with “everything immutable on-chain.”

### 27. Are FeeRouter **100% / 45% / 55%** “how a travel order splits payment”?

**No—that is not trip settlement.** In public materials, **100% / 45% / 55%** only describe the **first-layer story for allocatable platform order fees** (FeeRouter). **Escrow principal for trips, traveler pay rails, and whether TTG is default checkout** are **not** defined by those three lines. **Gas, arbitration economics, and slashing** use **different denominators**—do **not** blend them into one spoken “payment split.” Details: **[06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md) Section 06**.

### 28. Isn’t “Stripe / acquirer + escrow” enough?

**Not as a one-liner substitute for this product arc.** Funds often mean **Stripe Connect**-class rails for **money-in / chargebacks / KYC**. TravelTrust’s public story is a **travel-order** state machine across **quote → milestones → fulfillment → dispute → release**, with **evidence**, plus **separate disclosure rails** for **trip principal**, **allocatable platform fees (FeeRouter layer 1)**, and **governance (TTG)**. **One-line public boundary:** acquirer + custody answers “how money moves”; it does **not** by itself ship a **single order ID** **fulfillment + dispute + reputation** stack. See **[06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md) §1.3** and the **Web2 OTA / typical on-chain pay wallet / TravelTrust** comparison table.

### 29. Why chain at all (vs a company database + lawyers)?

The public claim is **crypto-native constraints** on **high-dispute-value** steps so release/refund and dispute paths are **third-party replayable** in principle (deployment/version per public releases). **One-line public boundary:** chain modules are not “a cooler database”; they anchor **auditable execution boundaries** for the contested path—**[06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md) §1.3**.

### 30. Can we bolt together seven vertical SaaS tools instead?

**Rarely as a clean substitute for one travel-order spine.** Point tools often cover **payments, ticketing, CRM, recon** separately while still missing a coherent **evidence → escrow → dispute → reputation** thread under **one trip order ID**; integration also carries **embed cutover + disclosure alignment + training** costs. **One-line public boundary:** read the Pitch **competitive matrix** slide; switching discipline in **[06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md) §10.2**.

### 31. If TTG isn’t trip pay, how do we talk about “crypto upside” in public?

**Public pack: boundaries and tool roles only—no valuation multiples or “up-only” claims.** TTG (if any) is framed around **governance voting/delegation and ecosystem-budget process**—**not** default checkout or Escrow settlement asset; keep it separate from guide-side staking rails (**FAQ #16**). **One-line public boundary:** do not verbally collapse **governance tooling** into a **“trip yield coin”** story; Web3-aware pack readers may open **07-Protocol-Tokenomics** alongside **06 §07**—still **not an offer**.
